source_text:
Ἔστι γοῦν ἐννοοῦντας ἰδεῖν ὅπως ὀνόματι μὲν αὐτὰ τὰ τῶν πειρασμῶν πάθη κλιμακτῆρας ἔσθ' ὅτε κικλήσκουσί τινες ἀμφικρήμνους
ἀναβάσεις ὑπεμφαίνοντα καὶ καταβάσεις, σχήματι δὲ τῷ σταυρῷ προσέοικεν ὀλίγως πως ἡ κλῖμαξ, ὀρθίοις τε καὶ πλαγίοις ἁρμοσθεῖσα ξύλοις. Ὡς οὖν ἱστόρησε τὴν τοιαύτην ὀπτασίαν, τὸν λίθον ἄρας, ἐφ' ᾧ τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀνακλίνας ἡσύχασεν, ἔστησε μὲν αὐτὸν εἰς στήλην ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἱστορίας, εἰκόνα δὲ τοῦ φανέντος αὐτῷ προσώπου χαρακτηρίζων, ἐν ᾧ μνήμης ἀνανέωσιν ἵδρυσεν, οἶκον δὲ Θεοῦ προσειπὼν αὐτὸν, ᾐνίττετο τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγου ναὸν ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξέφηνεν ὁ τοῦ Παντοκράτορος Υἱός· λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν. Ἤδη δὲ καὶ πύλην ὠνόμασεν οὐρανοῦ τὸν αὐτὸν, ἐπειδὴ διὰ τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ναουργίας τὸ σῶμά τε καὶ ψυχὴν καθαριζόμενοι, τῇ θείᾳ δυνάμεθα προσιέναι φύσει.
thought_title: The ladder's shape and the stone as temple and gate
orientation: Eustathius is explaining how the details of Jacob's vision and pillar at Bethel prefigure Christ, the cross, and the church.
pass_a_gloss: It is possible, then, for those who consider it to see how by name some people sometimes call the very sufferings of temptations steep rugged ascents and descents, but in shape the ladder resembles the cross somewhat, fitted together with upright and crosswise timbers. When therefore he had beheld such a vision, he took up the stone on which he had reclined his head and rested, and he set it up as a pillar as a memorial of the event, and as a likeness representing the face that had appeared to him, in which he established a renewal of memory, and calling it house of God, he was hinting at the house of God, the temple of the Word of God, as also the Son of the Almighty himself declared: destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it. And already he also named the same stone gate of heaven, since through the temple-building of Christ, being cleansed in body and soul, we are able to approach the divine nature.

lemmas.gloss: with cliffs on both sides, rugged
was hinting at, was speaking in riddles

choices.why: The word is a rare noun from κλῖμαξ (ladder), used here for the steep, cliff-lined paths of temptations; rendering it as 'steep rugged ascents' preserves the sense of dangerous climbing paths without importing 'ladder' where the author distinguishes name from shape.
The phrase describes paths with cliffs on both sides, conveying the perilous nature of temptations; 'rugged' captures the craggy, precipitous quality of ἀμφικρήμνους.
rejected: cliff-lined goings up and goings down

choices.term: ὀρθίοις τε καὶ πλαγίοις ἁρμοσθεῖσα ξύλοις
choices.english: fitted together with upright and crosswise timbers
choices.why: The literal description of the ladder's construction as upright and crosswise timbers directly evokes the shape of the cross, which is the author's point; 'timbers' renders ξύλοις concretely.
rejected: vertical and horizontal pieces of wood

choices.term: εἰκόνα δὲ τοῦ φανέντος αὐτῷ προσώπου χαρακτηρίζων
choices.english: and as an image characterizing the face that had appeared to him
choices.why: The participle χαρακτηρίζων is active: Jacob is making the stone into an image that bears the character of the face he saw; the rendering keeps the active force and the sense of imprinting a likeness.
rejected: as an image of the face that appeared to him
depicting the face that had appeared

choices.why: The rare noun ναουργία means the act of building or constructing a temple; rendering it as 'temple-building' preserves the active, constructive sense tied to Christ's body as the temple.

choices.english: we are able to approach the divine nature
choices.why: The infinitive προσιέναι with δυνάμεθα expresses ability to approach; 'the divine nature' renders θείᾳ φύσει literally, preserving the theological claim about access to God.
rejected: we can draw near to the divine nature
we are able to come to the divine nature

bible_refs.note: λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν

pass_b_english: So if we think about it, we can see that some people sometimes call the very sufferings of temptations by the name of steep rugged ascents and descents, paths with cliffs on both sides. Yet in shape the ladder does in some small way resemble the cross, fitted together with upright and crosswise timbers. When Jacob had beheld this vision, he took the stone on which he had reclined his head and rested, and he set it up as a pillar as a memorial of the event. He also made it an image characterizing the person who had appeared to him, and in it he established a renewal of remembrance. By calling it the house of God, he was hinting at the temple of God's Word, as the Son of the Almighty himself declared: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up" (John 2:19). He also named the same stone the gate of heaven, because through the temple-building of Christ we are cleansed in body and soul, and so we are able to approach the divine nature.

problems.quote: the face that had appeared to him
problems.why: πρόσωπον here means 'person' not 'face'; Christ appeared as a person, not a face.
problems.fix: the person who had appeared to him
problems.ruling: φανέντος προσώπου: in a theophany πρόσωπον means 'person' not 'face'; Christ appeared as a person, not merely a face.

edits.old: the face that had appeared to him
edits.new: the person who had appeared to him

problems.why: Three related terms for same concept may confuse: house of God, temple, temple-building.
problems.fix: Clarify these are equivalent or use one term.

problems.quote: fitted together with upright and crosswise timbers
problems.why: Ladders don't have 'timbers'; this describes a cross, not a ladder, confusing the simile.
problems.fix: Clarify: the cross resembles a ladder in shape, having upright and crosswise beams.

problems.quote: he established a renewal of remembrance
problems.why: Nonsensical phrase; 'renewal of remembrance' is contradictory or tautological.
problems.fix: Likely means 'a new way of remembering' or 'a memorial for future generations.'

problems.why: Obscure compound; likely means 'Christ's body as temple' or 'temple built by Christ'.
problems.fix: Clarify meaning: 'through Christ's body as temple' or 'through Christ's temple-building work.'

edits.old: Yet in shape the ladder does in some small way resemble the cross, fitted together with upright and crosswise timbers.
edits.new: Yet in shape the ladder does in some small way resemble the cross, being fitted together with upright and crosswise beams.

edits.old: and in it he established a renewal of remembrance.
edits.new: and in it he established a memorial for future remembrance.

edits.old: because through the temple-building of Christ we are cleansed in body and soul
edits.new: because through Christ's body as a temple we are cleansed in body and soul

fixed: The glossary issue about house of God, temple, and temple-building is addressed by clarifying in the gloss that the house of God is the temple of the Word of God, and by rendering 'temple-building of Christ' as 'Christ's body as a temple' in the English.
The phrase 'fitted together with upright and crosswise timbers' was changed to 'beams' to avoid the implication that ladders have timbers, while preserving the cross-like shape.
The phrase 'a renewal of remembrance' was changed to 'a memorial for future remembrance' to convey the sense of establishing a lasting memorial.
The obscure compound 'temple-building of Christ' was clarified as 'Christ's body as a temple' to express the intended meaning.

problems.why: First called 'victory-bearing trophy' then simply 'the cross'; reader may miss they're identical.
Three terms for same concept: house of God, temple of God's Word, Christ's body as temple.
problems.fix: Clarify these are synonymous or pick one.

problems.quote: some people sometimes call the very sufferings of temptations by the name of steep rugged ascents and descents, paths with cliffs on both sides
problems.why: Sentence introduces a topic (sufferings as ascents/descents) then abandons it for ladder-cross comparison.
problems.fix: Delete or connect to ladder imagery explicitly.

problems.quote: an image characterizing the person who had appeared to him
problems.fix: 'a likeness representing the one who had appeared'.

problems.quote: the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand
problems.why: 'Pre-painted beforehand' is awkward; likely means 'prefigured' or 'foreshadowed.'

edits.old: an image characterizing the person who had appeared to him
edits.new: a likeness representing the one who had appeared to him

fixed: The glossary problems about 'victory-bearing trophy, the cross' and 'the house of God' do not appear in the current English text; the English already uses 'cross' and 'house of God' consistently, so no edit is needed.

The unreadable sentence about 'steep rugged ascents and descents, paths with cliffs on both sides' is a faithful rendering of the source and is not abandoned; it is the first half of the contrast with the ladder's shape, so no edit is needed.
The phrase 'the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand' does not appear in the current English text, so no edit is needed.
